blocks.text: `-v` and `--mount` configure the same mounts; `--mount` is explicit and fails loudly, while `-v` infers the type and silently creates missing bind sources.

rows: Inferred: name → volume, path → bind, none → anonymous

items: From `-v /path` or an image VOLUME with nothing mounted; random 64-hex names.
`docker rm -v` or `--rm` removes them; plain `docker rm` leaves them behind.
Compose reattaches a service's anonymous volumes on recreate: stale `.venv`/`node_modules` after rebuild (fix with `-V`).

blocks.text:
$ docker volume ls
$ docker volume inspect rag_pgdata
$ docker volume rm rag_pgdata        # fails if any container (even stopped) uses it
$ docker volume prune                # unused anonymous volumes; -a adds named

items: Named volumes survive `docker rm`, `compose down` (without -v) and `system prune` (without --volumes).
Compose prefixes volume names with the project name; renaming the folder creates a new, empty volume.

blocks.text: Q: "Why prefer --mount in scripts?" A: "Because a typo in a -v bind source silently creates an empty root-owned directory and the app starts with no config, while --mount fails with 'bind source path does not exist'."

items: Anonymous volumes leak and get reattached by Compose.
Named volumes survive almost everything but -v/--volumes.
Stable Compose project names keep volume names stable.
